newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks a good buy as economy firms - DBS.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks a good buy as economy firms - DBS.

text.p: Singapore equities are on the brink of recovery as the economic outlook improves in the second half of the year and regional currency volatility recedes, DBS Investment Research director Mano Sabnani said on Thursday.
The stock market stands to capture more interest as recent sterling performers, such as property investments, stay depressed, he said.

"The market could recover about 25 percent for the next six to nine months starting in October," Sabnani told investors over lunch. Many stocks were trading at the lower end of their valuations, Sabani said.
He said the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) would crawl out of its 1,900-2,100 trading band in the fourth quarter and could rise as high as 2,500 points.
The STII sank to its lowest level since 1995 in mid-July, dragged down by weak confidence in Asia and the flight of foreign funds on concerns over Thailand's economic woes and regional currencies.
But Sabnani said he based his sanguine outlook on the assumption that volatile regional currency markets were in the process of stabilising.
He said recent speculative attacks on the Singapore dollar were more a function of the lack of central bank intervention than poor fundamentals.
The Singapore dollar's slide to a low of 1.47 against the U.S. dollar could in fact boost market sentiment as a softer currency would help exporters, he said.
Singapore's electronics sector, which makes up a hefty 70 percent of exports, should also enjoy better demand as U.S. orders for electronic components picks up and filters through.
Sabani said investors were likely to stay sidelined ahead of the corporate reporting season in September but the overall market should benefit from improved liquidity later.
The DBS report said some newly-listed stocks held promise, U.S. dollar stocks listed locally could gain from a strong currency, and electronic issues rise on the back of the sector's recovery.
And the foreign exchange risk of the Singapore dollar was limited, given a Singapore $115 billion foreign reserve and a current account surplus, Sabani said.
"We expect the fall of the Singapore dollar to stabilise around these levels," he said.
An economic recovery was also well underway and would gather steam into the second half of the year, he added.
A DBS Investment Research forecast gross domestic product (GDP) would steadily rise and see an average of 6.2 percent for 1997.
Sabnani said a lack of pressure on interest rates was also favourable to the stock market.
"The turnaround has begun. It began on July 17 when the market reached 1,920," he said. Now was the time to pick up good quality stocks which had fallen to attractive levels, he said.

DBS recommended buys on issues like automotive parts firm GPE Industries due to its investments in China, printed circuit board maker Gul Technologies because of major expansion plans and Hotel Properties, on its property earnings and foreign hotel prospects.
